skill.name: lint-typecheck
skill.description: Run frontend ESLint and TypeScript checks, then report lint warnings, lint errors, and type errors with file locations.
skill.summary: Validate frontend lint and TypeScript status before commits.
skill.author: AppleLamps

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline command examples in SKILL.md. The skill describes standard lint and TypeScript checks and includes a guardrail requiring confirmation before auto-fixes.

static_findings.snippet: - Offer to fix auto-fixable ESLint issues: `npm run lint -- --fix`

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 11 is a Markdown bash code fence, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The fenced command is a documented lint command, not dynamic code execution.
Line 13 is the closing Markdown code fence for the lint example. It does not execute a command or interpolate user input.
Line 16 is a Markdown bash code fence before a TypeScript check example. The text documents a fixed command and is not executable Ruby backtick syntax.
Line 18 is a closing Markdown code fence. It is formatting only and provides no command execution path.
Line 22 contains an inline Markdown command example for ESLint auto-fix. The skill also says auto-fix should only run with user confirmation.

content.value_statement: Frontend changes can introduce lint warnings and TypeScript errors before review. This skill runs standard checks and reports actionable results.
actual_capabilities: Runs the frontend ESLint command from the project directory.
Runs TypeScript build checking without emitting compiled files.
Reports lint warnings, lint errors, and type errors separately.
Lists errors with file locations when checks fail.
Offers ESLint auto-fix only after user confirmation.
limitations: It expects a frontend directory with npm scripts already configured.
It does not repair TypeScript errors automatically.
It does not change TypeScript configuration to hide errors.
It depends on the project's installed lint and TypeScript tooling.

use_cases.title: Pre-Commit Validation
use_cases.description: Run lint and type checks before committing frontend changes.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Check whether a branch has lint or type problems before review.

use_cases.title: Refactor Verification
use_cases.description: Confirm that a TypeScript refactor did not break static checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the frontend lint and type checks. Report warnings, lint errors, and type errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard validation pass.

prompt_templates.title: Check Before Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the frontend before I commit. Include file locations for every reported issue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wants a clean status before version control work.

prompt_templates.title: Review Type Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the TypeScript check and summarize each type mismatch with the affected file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer is focused on type safety after code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Triage and Fix Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint and type checks. If ESLint can auto-fix issues, ask before applying fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow that separates diagnosis from changes.

output_examples.output: Lint completed with two warnings and no errors. The warnings are listed by file for follow-up.

output_examples.input: Check for type errors before commit.
output_examples.output: Type checking found one mismatch in a component prop. The report names the file and expected type.

output_examples.input: Validate the frontend and fix safe lint issues.
output_examples.output: The check found auto-fixable lint issues. The assistant asks for confirmation before applying changes.

best_practices: Run checks before opening or updating a pull request.
Review the full issue list before applying auto-fixes.
Fix TypeScript errors directly instead of suppressing compiler settings.
anti_patterns: Do not run auto-fixes without user approval.
Do not ignore reported file locations during triage.
Do not change TypeScript configuration only to silence errors.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It runs frontend ESLint and TypeScript checks, then summarizes warnings and errors.

faq.question: Does it modify files?
faq.answer: It starts in read-only mode and only offers ESLint fixes after user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it fix TypeScript errors?
faq.answer: It identifies type mismatches, but the user or assistant must make the code changes.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: It uses the project's npm lint script and TypeScript compiler check.

faq.question: Does it work outside frontend projects?
faq.answer: It is designed for repositories with a frontend directory and configured npm scripts.

faq.question: Is it useful before commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It is intended to validate frontend code before commits or reviews.
